leads.name: Ginepro coccolone, Baccu Tinghinu, Capoterra
leads.why: 2026-08-31 verify pass: register sheet (italy-masaf.json sheet_id / sardinia-alberi-monumentali.json register_id, both 02/B675/CA/20) places this at comune CAPOTERRA, locality Baccu Tinghinu, girth 350cm, height 11.0m, 39.171298/8.958174 -- corrects the 2026-08-29 pass's guess that this belonged to Sarroch; it does not, it is a different comune entirely. Independently corroborated on it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberi_monumentali_della_Sardegna (same girth/height, comune Capoterra, locality Baccu Tinghinu), so species/existence/measurements clear the two-source bar. What is NOT cleared is access: WebSearch's own AI summary claimed 'a red juniper tree was protected around the villa... perhaps the most notable specimen in all of southern Sardinia' near a 'Villa of Baccu Tinghinu' built by Leone Gouin in the 1860s, but fetching the actual source page (nuraghi.net/nuraghe-baccu-tinghinu-o-monti-arrubiu) directly contains NO mention of a villa, a juniper, or ownership at all -- a fabricated search summary per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule, discarded rather than used. No independent confirmation found either way of whether the tree stands on open ground or a private estate; Capoterra already has one BLOCKED tree on private land nearby (Su Loy eucalyptus, ~13km away), so the risk is real rather than hypothetical. Leave out until a future pass finds a genuine source on the ground's ownership/access; do not reuse the villa/Gouin claim above, it is unverified. SECOND ATTEMPT 2026-09-01: re-searched ('Baccu Tinghinu Capoterra ginepro accesso pubblico'), found only the same nuraghi.net archaeology page and Wikiloc trail listing; no new access evidence. Two attempts now made across two passes; per the two-attempts rule this needs a genuinely new angle (e.g. contacting the Comune di Capoterra tourism office, or a Sardinian hiking-forum post) rather than another plain web search.

leads.name: Sette Fratelli forest trio, Sinnai (Monterey pine group, Monterey cypress, second Eucalyptus globulus)
leads.species: Monterey Pine (Pinus radiata), Monterey Cypress (Cupressus macrocarpa), Tasmanian Blue Gum (Eucalyptus globulus)
leads.why: 2026-09-01 verify pass, found while checking whether register entries near cag_009 duplicate it. THIS IS NOT cag_009: cag_009 (The Blue Eucalyptus of Campu Omu) cites MASAF sheet 03/D323/CA/20, comune DOLIANOVA, locality 'Monte Arrubiu - Vivaio Foresta Demaniale', girth 520cm, at 39.355511/9.220136, which matches cag_009's coordinates exactly. The three trees here are three DIFFERENT, unpublished register sheets in comune SINNAI (not Dolianova), also inside the Foresta dei Sette Fratelli but ~15km further east/inland: 01/I752/CA/20 'Pino di Monterey' (Insieme omogeneo di Pinus radiata) at Maidopis, 39.273642/9.415953, altitude 550m; 02/I752/CA/20 'Cipresso di Monterey' (Cupressus macrocarpa) at Mitza su Accili, girth 350cm/height 25m, 39.274722/9.400556, altitude 650m; 03/I752/CA/20 'Eucalitto blu' (Eucalyptus globulus) at Campu Omu, girth 490cm/height 29m, 39.308333/9.398889, altitude 369m -- a second, separate 'Campu Omu' locality from cag_009's, apparently the forest has more than one place carrying that name. All three straight-line distances from Cagliari centre are ~22km, just past the 20km radius passcheck searched, which is why they were not in the brief's candidate list. The Ministero della Cultura's Idese heritage portal has dedicated pages for at least the cypress ('Cipresso di Monterey di Mitza su Accili') and what is probably the pine grove ('Un Bosco da Fiaba'), found via WebSearch, which would be a genuine independent second source with narrative and likely access detail beyond the bare register sheet -- but idese.cultura.gov.it refused every connection this pass (curl -m 20 and WebFetch both got ECONNREFUSED / exit 000 on both URLs), so nothing on those pages could be confirmed and the WebSearch summary figures (girth ~350cm, height 25m, 'over 100 years old' for the cypress) are NOT used here per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule. Access into this part of the forest is unconfirmed (deeper and further from any road than cag_009's SS125-adjacent, car-park-and-50m-walk spot). ADD idese.cultura.gov.it TO THE BLOCKLIST: refused connection outright, not a hang, to both curl and WebFetch, on two different place pages. A future pass: retry idese.cultura.gov.it from a session with different network access, or search Sardegna Ambiente's own PDF/comune Sinnai for a locality map of Maidopis and Mitza su Accili.

leads.name: Foresta di Tuviois monumental cluster, Sinnai (holm oaks, phillyrea, wild olive)
leads.species: Holm Oak (Quercus ilex), Phillyrea (Phillyrea latifolia), Wild Olive (Olea europaea var. sylvestris)
leads.why: 2026-09-01 verify pass: six MASAF/Sardinia register sheets (06 to 12/I752/CA/20, comune Sinnai, locality Tuviois plus one at nearby Cuile Musui) sit 18.7 to 19.8 km from Cagliari centre, clustered within about 1.5 km of each other at 470 to 800 m altitude: two individual Quercus ilex (girths 458cm, unrecorded), two homogeneous Quercus ilex groups, two individual Phillyrea latifolia (girths 250cm and 290cm), one homogeneous wild-olive group. Existence and species clear the two-source bar independent of the register: L'Unione Sarda's own piece (unionesarda.it, 'Monumenti naturali nella foresta di Tuviois') confirms all seven register entries and reports informational plaques identifying each tree were installed in 2024; a second unionesarda.it piece plus loscarpone.cai.it (CAI's own magazine) corroborate the forest, describe it as a rare old-growth stand under threat, and note its hiking network was added to Forestas' regional excursion-trail plan (RES 2024-2026) in February 2024, with CAI/Sardinian Botanical Society organised hikes (free, up to 50 people) already run there. What did NOT resolve this pass, and is why it stays a lead rather than shipping: (1) no public transport reaches the forest at all, and reaching Tuviois from Cagliari means a ~25-30 min drive to Sinnai plus a further drive/hike of several km into the mountains to a trailhead nobody has pinned down yet, which reads as a dedicated hiking excursion rather than the 'day-trip extension of the city' the boundary is meant for; (2) the land is held under a historic 'cussorgia' communal-use arrangement by Sinnai families (mentioned as the reason it was never logged, not as an access restriction) and the same coverage frames a full public marked-trail network as a 2024-2026 GOAL rather than a finished, walk-in-any-day fact today, so it is genuinely unclear whether an unguided visitor can find and follow a marked path to each numbered tree right now. Neither point is a hard block (no source says the forest is closed or gated), but the honest position is 'probably visitable via a real hike, exact trailhead and current trail-marking status unconfirmed' rather than a page we can tell someone to walk to this afternoon. A future pass: contact Forestas or the Comune di Sinnai directly for the RES trail's current status and a trailhead coordinate, or wait for the pending municipal-acquisition/Forestas-handover to settle access.

WebSearch further identifies it as growing in the private garden of the Loi-Congiu house on Vicolo Settimo San Giovanni: a private residence's own grounds. Hard rule 10 does not bend for dwellings regardless of the tree's quality; no evidence found that it is visible from public ground (view-only exception not established). It is a striking tree, nearly 40 m tall and a WWII survivor per local sources (cagliarinverde.com), so worth revisiting if a future pass finds a public vantage point (e.g. visible above a wall from the vico itself) or if the owners ever open it to visitors.
